title: Sake–Yuzu Cucumber Cocktail
headnote: DRAFT / UNTESTED REVISED FORMULA — October 5, 2026 experiment. Earlier version was tasted and described as not sweet enough; latest proposed revision below was not confirmed as tested. Makes one cocktail.

ingredientGroups.title: Latest proposed build
items: 5–7.5 ml gin (restrained; 15 g was too strong in earlier trial)
20–22 g yuzu honey tea (jarred yuzu-honey preserve)
Tiny pinch salt or 2 drops saline solution

ingredientGroups.title: Optional bergamot-free alternative (not part of the main recipe)
items: Use 22–25 g yuzu honey tea instead of 20–22 g

steps: Muddle 12 g cucumber gently in a shaker to release its juice and aroma.
Add sake, restrained amount of gin, lemon juice, bergamot syrup, yuzu honey tea, and a tiny amount of salt or saline.
Add ice and shake vigorously until chilled and the yuzu-honey preserve is fully dispersed.
Double-strain over fresh ice into a chilled rocks glass.
Garnish with a cucumber slice and expressed/twisted lemon peel. Taste and adjust the next build for sweetness and acidity.
reviewFlags: DRAFT — this is the latest proposed revision, not a verified successful final drink.
October 5 initial tested build: 60 ml sake, 15 ml lemon, 15 ml bergamot syrup, 9 g cucumber, ½ tbsp yuzu-honey tea. User reported it was not sweet enough.
Gin at 15 g was reported too strong. Keep it restrained at approximately 5–7.5 ml (the user's accepted range was 5–10 g).
